title: Constructible derived comparison for arbitrary finite rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $B$ a finite commutative ring. Use the small etale and pro-etale sites, their coefficient sheaves, and the exact derived inverse image $\nu_X^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The functor $\nu_X^*$ induces an equivalence between bounded etale complexes with constructible cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and pro-etale complexes whose cohomology is intrinsically constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] and vanishes outside a finite interval. It preserves and reflects each cohomological interval $[a,b]$. In particular every such pro-etale complex has bounded constructible etale origin. No assumption that $B$ is a quotient of a discrete valuation ring is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived (and exact cohomology comparison); applies to every Noetherian ring, hence every finite ring

proof.text: Factor the specified intrinsic inverse image as fixed-module inverse image C followed by intrinsic realization R. The realization is an exact equivalence. Its sheafification counit gives R(U(M)) isomorphic to M for restriction U to constant scalars. Full faithfulness of R then gives U(R(G)) isomorphic to G. The restriction constructibility comparison identifies intrinsic constructibility of R(G) with fixed-module constructibility of G, retaining the global finite partitions. The etale constructibility comparison likewise identifies the source predicates.

Every source object is bounded below. Restrict the existing fixed-module derived Hom bijection to this full subcategory to obtain fullness and faithfulness. Compose with the derived realization equivalence and transport across mapDerivedCategoryCompIso.

Use the finite-level comparison theorem for exactness of C, retaining the comparison-morphism unit step. Exact cohomology comparison identifies H^i(F(L)) with F(H^i(L)). Fixed-module comparison preserves constructibility, and realization preserves the intrinsic predicate by step 1. Isomorphism invariance then proves that any object in the specified essential image has constructible cohomology and the same finite cohomological bounds.

Conversely transfer K to J under the derived realization equivalence. Exactness and faithfulness reflect its cohomological bounds. Step 1 transfers each intrinsic cohomology predicate to fixed-module constructibility. Descend each cohomology sheaf using fixed-module constructible origin. Apply the existing boundedConstructible_of_homology theorem to obtain a bounded constructible etale origin L of J. Convert the etale constructibility predicate, replace separate lower and upper bounds by their minimum and maximum, and compose the comparison and realization isomorphisms to obtain the required origin of K.

For any etale complex, exact intrinsic inverse image preserves zero cohomology and faithful intrinsic inverse image reflects zero cohomology. Apply these facts degreewise outside any requested interval, including an empty interval. Faithfulness follows from the underived comparison unit and the realization equivalence.
